name: ECS Cluster
description: Logical grouping of tasks/services + the capacity infrastructure they run on. Default cluster auto-created; production usage typically per-environment (prod/staging/dev) or per-team. Cluster scopes IAM, capacity-provider strategies, and account-settings opt-ins.

name: Fargate launch type
description: Serverless — AWS owns the underlying compute. Pay per task vCPU+memory+ephemeralStorage per second. Networking REQUIRES awsvpc. Restrictions: no privileged containers, no host networking, restricted sysctls, restricted Linux capabilities, no host volumes (only EFS/FSx + ephemeralStorage). Per Cognition's NSDI-paper analog: each Fargate task runs in its own Firecracker microVM (cross-domain link).

name: Fargate Spot
description: Spot-priced Fargate. ~70% discount vs on-demand. AWS may interrupt with a SIGTERM-then-2-minute-warning. Use via capacityProviderStrategy mixing FARGATE + FARGATE_SPOT (e.g. base=2 on FARGATE, weight 1:9 FARGATE:FARGATE_SPOT). Best for fault-tolerant async workloads.

name: EC2 launch type
description: User manages container instances (EC2 instances running ECS-optimized AMI + amazon-ecs-agent). Required for: privileged containers, host network mode, custom AMIs, GPU/Inferentia/Trainium hardware, capacity reservations, .metal instances, ECS Anywhere. Pay for EC2 instances regardless of task density.

name: External launch type (ECS Anywhere)
description: ECS orchestration on customer-managed on-prem or other-cloud machines. Each external instance runs amazon-ecs-agent + SSM Agent + activation token. Limitations: no awsvpc network mode, no Service Connect, no Capacity Providers (manage capacity yourself).

name: ECS Managed Instances
description: AWS fully manages the underlying EC2 instances (provisioning, patching, scaling) while preserving more control than Fargate (e.g., GPU support, custom AMIs from a curated set). Newer (mid-2024) middle option between Fargate and EC2-launch-type. Promoted as the recommended option for most clusters.

name: Capacity Provider
description: Decouples 'where do tasks run' from 'what launch type are they'. Built-in: FARGATE, FARGATE_SPOT. EC2: bind to an ASG (Auto Scaling Group) — managedScaling enables ECS to drive ASG up/down based on task demand. Cluster has a default strategy; services + run-task can override.

name: Managed Scaling (CP-driven ASG)
description: ECS publishes a CloudWatch metric (CapacityProviderReservation = active-tasks / target-capacity * 100) that the ASG's TargetTrackingScalingPolicy reacts to. targetCapacity (default 100%) lets the cluster keep slack for fast scale-out. instanceWarmupPeriod governs how long until a new instance counts as 'available'.

name: Capacity Provider strategy (base + weight)
description: {capacityProvider, weight, base}. base = first N tasks placed on this CP unconditionally. weight = ratio for tasks beyond base. e.g. [{cp:FARGATE,base:2,weight:1},{cp:FARGATE_SPOT,base:0,weight:9}] → first 2 tasks on FARGATE, then 1:9 split. Enables cost-tier mixing.

name: ECS-optimized AMI family
description: AMI variants pre-loaded with Docker/containerd + amazon-ecs-agent + ecs-init. Variants: AL2023 (recommended; long-term-support through 2028), AL2 kernel 5.10 (EOL 2026-06-30), AL2023 arm64 (Graviton), AL2023 GPU (NVIDIA + Docker GPU runtime), AL2023 Neuron (Inferentia/Trainium). 30 GiB root volume default.

name: AMI ID via SSM Parameter Store
description: Latest ECS-optimized AMI ID is published as an SSM parameter (/aws/service/ecs/optimized-ami/<variant>/recommended/image_id). CloudFormation references this dynamic parameter so each stack-update picks up the newest AMI without code change. Same pattern works in Terraform via aws_ssm_parameter.

name: AMI 2-year deprecation default
description: All ECS-Optimized AMIs are auto-marked deprecated 2 years after creation. EC2 DescribeImages returns the deprecation status. Pinning to an old AMI ID risks silent-deprecation; use the SSM parameter approach.
